summary: Restyle the Bob pipeline web UI (tools/bob-pipeline/apps/web) so it visually follows the look and feel of Chakra UI Pro (neutral gray surfaces, a single teal/blue accent, Inter typography, subtle borders and shadows, consistent radii and focus rings). This is a visual-only change; behaviour, routes and data flow stay the same.
approach: The only website in the repo is the React + Vite + Tailwind CSS v4 dashboard in tools/bob-pipeline/apps/web. Rather than adopting Chakra UI itself (which would mean replacing Tailwind and rewriting every component, and Chakra UI Pro is a paid, proprietary kit), reproduce its visual language on the existing stack: (1) define a design-token layer in index.css using Tailwind v4 @theme (font, accent colour scale, neutral surface and border colours, radii, shadows, focus ring) and set base body styles there instead of in index.html; (2) restyle the shared primitives in components/ui.tsx (Button, StatusBadge, Card, ErrorBox) so every page inherits the new look; (3) restyle the app shell in Layout.tsx (header, nav, poller controls, warning banner); (4) sweep the pages and views (Dashboard, IssuePage, DependenciesPage, DependencyTable, LogView, views/*) replacing ad-hoc slate/emerald utility classes with token-based classes, and align hard-coded hex colours in DepGraph.tsx and TestPyramidView.tsx with the new palette; (5) load Inter from a self-hosted package (no external CDN) with the existing system font stack as fallback. Styling is already centralised in a handful of primitives plus utility classes, so a token-driven restyle touches presentation only and adds no new runtime framework.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Requires removing Tailwind and rewriting every component; much larger scope and risk for a styling request.

alternatives_considered.option: Use Chakra UI Pro templates verbatim
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Proprietary and licensed; we only emulate the visual style.

alternatives_considered.option: Use shadcn/ui or another Tailwind component kit
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Adds dependencies and generated component code when a token restyle of the existing primitives achieves the goal.

alternatives_considered.option: Restyle each page ad hoc without tokens
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Leads to drift and makes later theme tweaks (or dark mode) expensive.

components: Web app global styles (index.css, index.html) - add theme tokens, Inter font, base body styles; remove hard-coded body colour classes
Shared UI primitives (components/ui.tsx) - new button variants, badge palette, card, error box styling
App shell (components/Layout.tsx) - restyled header, nav, poller controls, warning banner, page container
Board page (pages/Dashboard.tsx) - filter pills, kanban columns, issue cards, idle list restyled
Issue detail page (pages/IssuePage.tsx, components/LogView.tsx, views/*) - tabs, panels, log view, markdown prose and diff views restyled
Dependencies page (pages/DependenciesPage.tsx, components/DependencyTable.tsx, components/DepGraph.tsx) - table, graph node/edge colours and container restyled
Test pyramid view (views/TestPyramidView.tsx) - level colour palette aligned with the new theme
Web app dependencies (apps/web/package.json, lockfile) - add self-hosted Inter font package
assumptions: "The website" means the Bob pipeline dashboard in tools/bob-pipeline/apps/web; there is no other web front end in the repo.
"In the style of pro.chakra-ui.com" means visual emulation (look and feel), not use of Chakra UI components or Pro assets/code.
Tailwind CSS v4 and the existing component structure are retained.
A light theme is the deliverable; dark mode is not required.
Inter via a maintained, OFL-licensed self-hosted package (e.g. @fontsource-variable/inter) is acceptable as a new dependency and passes the repo's dependency/vulnerability checks.
No automated UI tests exist, so verification is typecheck, build and visual review.

risks.risk: Ambiguous target ("website", "style of") leads to an interpretation the author did not intend
risks.mitigation: Record the interpretation in the PR; keep tokens centralised so the palette/accent can be changed quickly.

risks.risk: Chakra UI Pro is proprietary; copying its assets or markup could breach licensing
risks.mitigation: Emulate the general visual language only; do not copy Pro templates, code or assets.

risks.risk: Wide class-name sweep causes visual regressions (board columns, graph, prose tables)
risks.mitigation: Change primitives first, then pages one at a time; manually review each page and the build output.

risks.risk: New font dependency introduces supply-chain or licensing concern
risks.mitigation: Use a maintained OFL package, pin via lockfile, run dependency scan.

risks.risk: Colour changes reduce contrast or make status/edge/test-level colours indistinguishable
risks.mitigation: Check contrast against WCAG AA and keep distinct hues per status/edge/level.

risks.risk: Hard-coded hex colours in graph/pyramid are missed and look inconsistent
risks.mitigation: Explicitly include DepGraph.tsx and TestPyramidView.tsx in the sweep and grep for remaining slate- and hex usage.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The web UI defines a central set of theme tokens (font, accent colour scale, neutral surface/border colours, radii, shadows) in index.css, and the primitives and shell consume them rather than hard-coded one-off colours.
The app uses Inter (self-hosted, no external CDN request) as its primary font with a system-font fallback.
Button (default, primary, danger, ghost), StatusBadge (all eight statuses), Card and ErrorBox are restyled in a Chakra-Pro-like manner and have visible keyboard focus states.
The header/navigation in Layout.tsx is restyled (surface, border, active nav state, poller controls, warning banner) and remains functional and responsive.
Board, Issue and Dependencies pages all use the new look consistently, with no remaining old-style emerald/ad-hoc palette on primary actions or surfaces.
The dependency graph and test pyramid colours are aligned with the new palette while edge kinds and test levels remain visually distinguishable.
Text/background colour combinations used for body text, badges and buttons meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for normal text).
No behaviour, routing, API or data changes; npm run typecheck and npm run build in apps/web pass with no new warnings.
The UI renders correctly at common desktop widths and degrades acceptably (no horizontal page overflow other than the existing board scroll) at tablet/mobile widths.

open_questions: Should dark mode be included, or is a light theme sufficient for this issue?
Is a sidebar app shell (as in Chakra Pro dashboards) desired, or should the existing top header layout be retained and merely restyled? This plan assumes the top header is retained.
Is there a preferred accent colour (Chakra Pro's teal/blue) or should the existing emerald be kept as the brand colour?
